title: Representing Data: Bar Graphs, Histograms and Pie Charts
seo_title: Grade 7 Representing Data Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Draw a variety of graphs by hand or technology to display and interpret data, including bar graphs and double bar graphs, histograms with given and own intervals, and pie charts; critically read and interpret data represented in words, bar graphs, double bar graphs, pie charts and histograms.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 worksheets: bar graphs, grouped data, histograms and pie charts with degrees. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A bar graph compares categories; a histogram shows grouped numerical data with bars that touch.
  • In a pie chart, the whole circle is 360°. A sector of 90° is a quarter of the data.
  • Sector angle = fraction of the data × 360°.
  • Choose a graph that suits the data and the question.

Examples

Example

12 of 40 learners chose soccer

12/40 × 360°

Answer: 108°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the scaleCheck what each line is worth.
A group as one valueA group like 10–19 has many values.
100 for a pie chartUse 360°.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 7 say about representing data?
faq.a: Draw and interpret bar graphs, double bar graphs, histograms with given and own intervals, and pie charts.

faq.q: What is the difference between a bar graph and a histogram?
faq.a: A histogram groups numbers into intervals and its bars touch.

faq.q: How many degrees is half a pie chart?
When is a pie chart best?
faq.a: When you compare parts of a whole.

items.q: What percent of the learners take the bus?
items.e: Read the label on the Bus sector: 35%. (65% is everyone else, and 126 is the angle of the sector in degrees.)

items.q: What is the angle of the Walk sector?
items.e: 30% × 360° = 0,3 × 360° = 108°. (30° reads the percent as degrees, 10,8° puts the decimal point in the wrong place, and 252° is the rest of the circle.)

items.q: The class has 40 learners. How many take the bus?
items.e: 35% of 40 = 0,35 × 40 = 14 learners. (35 is the percent, 26 learners do not take the bus, and 140 forgets to divide by 100.)

items.q: What percent of the learners chose spring?
items.e: 40% + 25% + 20% = 85%. The whole circle is 100%, so spring is 100% − 85% = 15%. (275 subtracts from 360: percents add up to 100, not 360.)

items.q: What percent of Ethan’s day is school?
items.e: 90° ÷ 360° = 0,25 = 25%. (90 is the angle, and 6 is the number of hours.)

items.q: How many hours does Ethan sleep?
items.e: The whole day, 24 hours, is 360°, so 1 hour is 360° ÷ 24 = 15°. 135° ÷ 15° = 9 hours. (13,5 divides by 10, and 37,5 is the percent.)

items.q: Which sector is 18 of Ethan’s day?
items.e: 18 of 360° = 45°. The Sports sector is 45° (3 hours). (Homework is 30° and Other is 60°.)

items.q: A sector is 12,5% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
items.e: 12,5% × 360° = 0,125 × 360° = 45°. Check: 12,5% is 18, and 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. (4,5° puts the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: A sector of a circle graph has an angle of 54°. What percent is it?
items.e: 54° ÷ 360° = 0,15 = 15%. (54% reads the degrees as a percent.)

items.q: How many viewers watched by streaming?
items.e: 35% of 2 400 000 = 0,35 × 2 400 000 = 840 000 viewers. (84 000 and 8 400 000 have the place value wrong, and 1 560 000 is everyone else.)

items.q: How many more viewers watched on TV than on the radio?
items.e: TV − radio = 55% − 10% = 45%. 45% of 2 400 000 = 0,45 × 2 400 000 = 1 080 000 viewers. (45 is the difference in percent, 1 320 000 is the TV viewers only, and 108 000 has the place value wrong.)

items.q: A circle graph shows the ages of the 650 000 people in a city. The sector for children aged 0 to 14 is 18%. How many children is that?
items.e: 1% of 650 000 = 6 500. 18% = 18 × 6 500 = 117 000 people. (11 700 and 1 170 000 put the place value wrong, and 533 000 are the other 82%.)

items.q: In a survey of 1 000 000 people, 250 000 chose loons as their favourite bird. What is the angle of the loon sector?
Which graph is best to show what percent of a class gets to school each way?
items.e: The ways of getting to school are parts of one whole class. A circle graph shows parts of a whole.

items.q: Which data can NOT be shown well in a circle graph?
c: Sports learners play (can pick more than one)
items.e: If learners can pick more than one sport, the percents add up to more than 100%. A circle graph needs parts of one whole.

items.q: How many hours does Ravi sleep?
items.e: 24 hours = 360°, so 1 hour = 360° ÷ 24 = 15°. Sleep: 135° ÷ 15° = 9 hours. (13,5 divides by 10.)

items.q: What percent of Ravi’s day is school?
items.e: 90° ÷ 360° = 0,25 = 25%. (6 is the number of hours, and 90 is the angle.)

items.q: How many more hours does Ravi sleep than spend at school?
items.e: Sleep: 135° ÷ 15° = 9 hours. School: 90° ÷ 15° = 6 hours. 9 − 6 = 3 hours. (45 is the difference in degrees.)

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: He sleeps more than one-third of the day
He is at school for half the day
He is at school longer than he sleeps
items.e: One-third of the day is 120°. Sleep is 135°, more than 120°. School is 90°, a quarter. Homework is 15° = 1 hour.

items.q: Which school has more learners who walk?
items.e: School A: 25% of 400 = 100. School B: 40% of 250 = 100. The Walk sector is bigger at School B, but School B has fewer learners.

What percent of the learners take the bus?
items.e: Read the label on the Bus sector: 25%.

items.q: Which way of getting to school is used by the most learners?
items.e: The biggest sector has the biggest percent: Walk is 35%, more than Car (30%).

items.q: What percent of the learners do not walk to school?
What percent of the learners take the bus or ride a bike?
items.e: Add the two sectors: 25% + 10% = 35%.

items.q: What percent of the learners chose spring?
items.e: The sectors add up to 100%. 45% + 25% + 20% = 90%. 100% − 90% = 10%. (270 comes from 360 − 90: percents add up to 100, not 360.)

items.q: What percent of the learners chose basketball?
items.e: 30% + 25% + 15% + 10% = 80%. The whole circle is 100%, so basketball is 100% − 80% = 20%.

items.q: Which two subjects together make exactly half of the circle graph?
items.e: Half is 50%. Maths 20% + Science 30% = 50%. PE and Art = 40%, Science and PE = 55%, Maths and PE = 45%.

items.q: Which subject was chosen by one-quarter of the learners?
items.e: One-quarter is 25%. The PE sector is 25%.

items.q: Which sector is 110 of the circle graph?
items.e: 110 = 10%. The Music sector is 10%.

items.q: How many percent more learners chose apples than grapes?
items.e: Subtract: 40% − 15% = 25%. (55% adds the two sectors.)

items.q: How many learners take the bus?
items.e: 25% = 14. 14 of 80 = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 learners. (25 is the percent, not the number of learners.)

items.q: How many learners ride a bike?
items.e: 10% of 80 = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 learners.

items.q: How many learners walk?
How many more learners walk than ride a bike?
items.e: Walk: 36. Bike: 8. 36 − 8 = 28 learners. (35 is the difference in percent, not in learners.)

items.q: How many learners chose granola bars?
items.e: 1% of 200 = 2. 35% = 35 × 2 = 70 learners. (35 would be right only for 100 learners.)

items.q: How many learners chose yogurt?
How many learners chose fruit or yogurt?
How many learners chose lacrosse?
items.e: 10% of 60 = 6 and 5% of 60 = 3. 15% = 6 + 3 = 9 learners. (4 comes from 60 ÷ 15.)

items.q: How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: 40% = 0,4. 0,4 × 60 = 24 learners. (2,4 puts the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: 24 of the 60 learners in a survey chose soccer. What percent is that?
items.e: 2460 = 25 = 0,4 = 40%. (36 is the number of learners who did not choose soccer.)

items.q: All the angles at the centre of a circle graph add up to …
items.e: A circle graph is a whole circle, and a full turn is 360°. (100 is for percents.)

items.q: A sector is 25% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
items.e: 25% × 360° = 0,25 × 360° = 90°. A sector of 25% is NOT 25°: it is one-quarter of the circle, a right angle.

items.q: A sector is 50% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
A sector is 10% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
A sector is 20% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
A sector is 35% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
items.e: 35% × 360° = 0,35 × 360° = 126°. (12,6° puts the decimal point in the wrong place.)

items.q: A sector is 15% of a circle graph. What is its angle?
A sector of a circle graph has an angle of 90°. What percent is it?
items.e: 90° ÷ 360° = 0,25 = 25%. (90% reads the degrees as a percent.)

items.q: A sector of a circle graph has an angle of 72°. What percent is it?
A sector of a circle graph has an angle of 108°. What percent is it?

The pie chart shows the choices of 36 learners. How many chose pizza?
72 people were asked their favourite food. 12 said curry. What angle would this be on a pie chart?
The pie chart shows the choices of 90 learners. How many chose car?
The pie chart shows the choices of 36 learners. How many chose bus?
180 people were asked their favourite colour. 93 said green. What angle would this be on a pie chart?
120 people were asked how they travel to work. 20 said bike. What angle would this be on a pie chart?
120 people were asked how they travel to work. 27 said bus. What angle would this be on a pie chart?
Which graph is best to show what percent of Ravi’s R200 savings goes to each goal?
items.e: The goals are parts of one whole (R200). A circle graph shows parts of a whole.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the heights of 30 learners, grouped 140 to 150 cm, 150 to 160 cm and so on?
items.e: Height is continuous data grouped in equal intervals. A histogram shows this, with bars that touch.

items.q: Which graph is best to compare the favourite sports of the boys and the girls in a class?
items.e: There are two groups to compare in each category. A double (multiple) bar graph puts the two bars side by side.

items.q: Which graph is best to show how many learners in each grade walk, bike or take the bus, and each grade’s total?
items.e: In a stacked-bar graph, each bar is one grade. The parts of the bar show walk, bike and bus, and the whole bar shows the total.

items.q: Which graph is best to show the times of 50 runners in a 5 km race?
items.e: Time is continuous data. Grouping the times in equal intervals (20 to 25 minutes, 25 to 30 minutes …) and drawing a histogram shows how the times are spread.

items.q: Liam made a circle graph of his puppy’s mass each month. Why is this a poor choice?
c: The masses are not parts of a whole
items.e: Adding the masses from 12 months gives no useful whole. A broken-line graph shows how the mass changes.

items.q: What is missing from this circle graph?
items.e: Every sector is labelled, and the percents add up to 100%. But there is no title, so a reader cannot tell what the graph is about or who was asked.

items.q: Which list shows what every graph should have?
c: A title, labels and a source
items.e: A title says what the graph shows, labels name the categories and scale, and the source says where the data came from.

items.q: Where should the source of the data go?
items.e: The source, such as “Survey of 7B learners, October 2 026”, usually goes under the graph. It tells readers where the data came from and how much to trust it.

items.q: A bar graph will show values from 120 to 890. Which scale is best?
items.e: The scale must start at 0 and go past the biggest value, 890. Steps of 100 give 10 easy grid lines. (Going up by 1 needs 900 lines, and starting at 100 makes bars look wrong.)

items.q: How many more cans were collected in 2 026 than in 2 022?
items.e: 2 026: 2 750. 2 022: 2 500. 2 750 − 2 500 = 250 cans. (2 750 is the 2 026 total, and 100 is only the last year.)

items.q: By what percent did the number of cans grow from 2 022 to 2 026?
items.e: Growth = 250 cans. 250 ÷ 2 500 = 0,1 = 10%. (250% reads the cans as a percent, 25% divides by 1 000 instead of 2 500, and 100% would mean doubling: the steep line makes it look that way because the scale starts at 2 500.)

items.q: A poster says, “Our food drive more than doubled!” Is this supported?
items.e: Doubling 2 500 gives 5 000. The school collected 2 750, only 10% more. The scale starts at 2 500, so the line looks steeper than it is.

items.q: Which school has more learners who walk?
items.e: School A: 20% of 600 = 120. School B: 40% of 300 = 120. The Walk sector is twice as big at School B, but School B has half as many learners.

items.q: How many more learners take the bus at School A than at School B?
items.e: School A: 45% of 600 = 270. School B: 30% of 300 = 90. 270 − 90 = 180 learners. (15 is the difference in percent.)

items.q: In a random survey of 400 learners in a school board, 35% said they walk to school. The board has 18 000 learners. About how many of them walk?
items.e: Use the sample percent for the whole board: 35% of 18 000 = 0,35 × 18 000 = 6 300 learners. (140 is 35% of the 400 in the sample, and 11 700 are the ones who do not walk.)

items.q: A city has 750 000 adults. In a random survey of 1 500 of them, 42% said they skate in winter. About how many adults in the city skate?
items.e: 42% of 750 000 = 0,42 × 750 000 = 315 000 people. (630 is 42% of the sample, 31 500 has the place value wrong, and 435 000 are the other 58%.)

items.q: A bar graph’s scale is labelled 0, 10, 20, 100, 500, with equal spaces between the labels. Why is it misleading?
items.e: The space from 0 to 10 is the same as the space from 100 to 500, but one is 10 and the other is 400. Bars on this scale cannot be compared fairly.

items.q: An ad shows sales doubling with two loon pictures. The second loon is twice as wide and twice as tall. Why is this misleading?
c: The big loon looks 4 times as big
It should be 3 times as tall
items.e: Doubling both the width and the height makes the area 2 × 2 = 4 times as big. The eye sees the area, so sales look 4 times bigger instead of 2 times.

items.q: A newspaper circle graph of favourite summer activities says: camping 45%, swimming 35%, biking 30%. What is wrong?
items.e: 45 + 35 + 30 = 110. The sectors of a circle graph must add up to exactly 100%, so the graph cannot be right.
